The network

Three groups, each with a defined role. Certification, expertise and funding never sit in the same hands.

Get involved. Whoever you are, there's a specific way in.

Government

Certifies that a request is real, necessary, and meets code — the layer that has to sign off before anything else can happen.

Ministry

Certifies technical & regulatory compliance nationally — the specific ministry depends on the request's field.

Governorates & Districts

Lebanon's nine governorates and the 26 districts within them. Coordinates across municipalities in its region — read-only on funds and certification.

Municipality

Posts the request and delivers the work on the ground, once certified.

Experts

Matched to a request by field — the specific technical knowledge a problem needs, distinct from who implements or who pays.

Sponsors

Funding, direct to the solution — every pledge tracked from commitment to release, named or anonymous.

Organisations & Businesses

Local companies and civic groups funding a specific request.

NGOs

Mission-driven nonprofits, often funding within their own focus area.

Embassies

Government-to-government cultural or development funding.

Diaspora

Individuals and diaspora associations funding their hometowns.

Locals

Residents pooling small amounts toward a nearby request.

The network is the platform — funding is just one thread in it

A certified municipal problem needs two different things to become a finished, verified project: someone who knows how to solve it, and someone willing to pay for the solution. Manāra connects both, in the open, with every claim independently checked.

Four models, one network

Every side of Manāra runs on a model people already trust and understand — working together as one system, not four separate apps.

Report
Solve
Consumer — report it, see it move

Anyone can file a problem and immediately see how it's being handled — the experts matched to it, the funding behind it, every milestone as it clears. No black box, no waiting to hear back.

Government — oversight, automated

A live, CRM-style view into requests and the expert network that doesn't exist anywhere today. Matching algorithms surface the right certifying body automatically, instead of relying on manual coordination between departments.

Experts — set your price, pick your work

Organisations sign up once, then choose which requests fit their expertise and set their own price per project — no bidding wars, no waiting to be picked.

Sponsors — funding, fully verified

Full visibility into where the money goes, government sign-off before it moves, and residents confirming real progress on the ground — while sponsors earn genuine recognition for the problems they helped solve.

Put together, this is a system built on track record, not political pull: direct communication with government for residents, automated matching for government, an open marketplace for experts, and a trusted, verified fund for sponsors.

One platform. Every issue resolved. Trust built in the open.

Our values

What the mechanics on this page are actually in service of.

👁

Transparency

Every pledge, escrow state and milestone sits on one public ledger. Nothing about where the money went is held back from the people who gave it.

🛡

Non-partisanship

Certification runs on technical and regulatory review, not political or sectarian standing. No party, sect, or patron gets a faster lane.

👥

Community

A request only carries weight once residents have confirmed the need is real. The network follows the community — not the other way around.

⚖

Accountability

Sponsors, implementers and government branches all answer to the same public record. No side channel, for anyone.

How the money is actually verified

Six steps, each one checkable.

01 · INTAKE

A named, checkable need

Requests come from a registered municipality, a vetted NGO, or a recognised business partner — many grounded in a citizen report already confirmed by other affected residents.

02 · VETTING

Whole-partner review

Before a request goes live, the implementing partner is checked once — legal registration, past project record, references.

03 · ESCROW

Money moves, but doesn't land yet

Pledges sit in escrow held by an independent custodian — never a government account, never the implementer's — until a milestone is verified.

04 · VERIFICATION

A claim and a check are different steps

Evidence sits as "submitted" until an unaffiliated verifier confirms it. Only then does the ledger mark it verified and escrow release.

05 · OPEN LEDGER

Anyone can trace any lira

Funders — named or anonymous — see the same trail everyone else does. No private reporting track.

06 · DISPUTE

A report button that goes somewhere

Flags route to an independent oversight partner, not to the implementer being flagged.

Design constraint worth stating out loud: this platform should never claim that one specific dollar funded one specific brick. Pooled milestone funding is more honest, and more auditable, than manufacturing a person-to-person link that isn't really there.

For Municipalities

Post a costed, timelined request and let diaspora and local businesses fund it directly — outside your general budget, with public credit for every verified step.

  • Post a scoped request — description, budget, timeline, expected partners.
  • Get public credit on the Scoreboard the moment a milestone is verified.
  • Works even where your council has limited capacity — pair with a vetted NGO.
  • You never hold pledged funds — an independent custodian does.

For Organisations

NGOs and vetted local businesses — step in where councils can't, and turn a one-off repair into a standing, funded service.

  • Become the vetted fallback partner where a council is dissolved.
  • Turn services like recycling or solar maintenance into a subscription-funded line.
  • Build a public delivery record on the Scoreboard.
  • Get paid against delivery proof — pickup logs, meter readings — not promises.
